proof_nl:
Fix an integer n>1, and let t be any real number with (n-1)/n <= t < 1. Let k be any integer with 1 <= k <= n. We show that floor(k t) = k-1.

From t >= (n-1)/n, we get
k t >= k(n-1)/n = k - k/n.
Since k <= n, we have k/n <= 1, so k - k/n >= k-1. Therefore
k-1 <= k t.

On the other hand, t < 1 implies k t < k.
Thus
k-1 <= k t < k.
Because k-1 is an integer, this interval condition implies floor(k t) = k-1.

Since k was arbitrary in {1,2,...,n}, the conclusion holds for every such k.
solver_summary: For k<=n and t in [(n-1)/n,1), one has k-1 <= kt < k, hence floor(kt)=k-1.
vetter_reason: The proof directly establishes the stated floor identity for an arbitrary n>1, arbitrary t in [(n-1)/n,1), and arbitrary k with 1<=k<=n. The inequalities are correct and sufficient to conclude floor(k*t)=k-1. No semantic drift or dependency issue is present.
